patients.summary: Wildlife biologist with well-controlled generalized tonic-clonic seizures on levetiracetam and hypertension on lisinopril who joined in mid-2024. Survived pneumonic plague contracted on a New Mexico field assignment in December 2024, then ARDS after a cold-water submersion a year later; the practice has not seen him since April 2025.

documents.title: New patient intake call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller would like to establish with the practice. Moved his care from his old doctor's office, which is too far a drive now. Two daily meds, seizure med and a BP pill, both filled through mail order. Insurance BCBS, verified. Booked new pt visit 6/11 at 9:00. Asked him to sign a records release for the prior office; form emailed.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily

procedures.procedure: Office visit, new patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
38 y/o M here to set up primary care. Wildlife biologist, a lot of field time, sometimes weeks away on assignments.

Seizures: generalized tonic-clonic seizure disorder, on Keppra (levetiracetam) 1000 mg BID for years. Well controlled, no events he can recall in a long time; father also has epilepsy. Takes it reliably, uses a pill box. No mood change on it that he notices. Drives.

HTN: lisinopril 10 mg daily, no cough, no dizziness. Doesn't check at home.

PSH: tonsils out at 12, open appendectomy at 25.
FHx: father epilepsy + HTN; mother T2DM; paternal grandfather MI at 62.
SHx: married. Never a smoker. Two or three drinks a week, beer mostly. No drugs.
Allergies: NKDA.

ROS negative except as above.

Exam: well appearing. HEENT unremarkable, tonsils absent. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear both sides. Abd soft, healed RLQ incision, nontender. Ext warm, no swelling. Neuro: alert, fluent, CN grossly intact, strength and gait normal.
PHQ-2 0.

A/P
1. Seizure disorder, generalized TC, controlled. Continue levetiracetam 1000 BID. Will take over refills.
2. HTN on lisinopril 10. Reading borderline high today after a rushed drive in; prior office readings were at goal. No change, recheck at follow-up. CMP.
3. Health maintenance: CBC, lipids, A1c given mom's diabetes. One-time HIV and hep C screen, he agrees. Flu/COVID this fall. Records requested from prior PCP.
RTC 3 months for BP.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Theo, your blood work from Tuesday looks good. Kidney function and potassium are normal on the lisinopril, blood counts are normal, cholesterol is fine, and your A1c shows no sign of diabetes. HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. Nothing to change. See you in September.

documents.title: RE: Your lab results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Great, thanks for the quick turnaround.

documents.author: outside primary care
documents.body: Records from former primary care office, 2019 through early 2024 (14 pages). Office notes for hypertension on lisinopril 10 mg daily and generalized seizure disorder on levetiracetam 1000 mg twice daily, no breakthrough events documented. BP readings in the 120s-130s/70s-80s. Yearly basic chemistry normal. Tdap given 2020. Allergies: none known. Filed; reviewed by PCP, nothing outstanding.

documents.author: RN
documents.body: Mail-order pharmacy requesting new 90-day prescriptions: levetiracetam 1000 mg BID and lisinopril 10 mg daily. Seen 6/11, labs normal. Sent 90 days with 3 refills each per protocol.

documents.title: Missed appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: We missed you yesterday for your 3:30 appointment. Please reply or call to reschedule.

documents.title: RE: Missed appointment
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Sorry, I was out at a field site with no service and lost track of the date. Could I just come in for the flu shot and a BP check in October instead?

documents.title: RE: Missed appointment
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: That works. Nurse visit in early October for vaccines and a pressure check.

documents.title: Nurse visit: vaccines and BP
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here for seasonal vaccines and a BP check in place of the missed September follow-up (June reading was borderline). Taking lisinopril every morning, no symptoms. Seated BP after 5 min within goal, reviewed with PCP who is fine to see him in the spring. Flu vaccine L deltoid, COVID R deltoid, lot numbers recorded. Observed 15 min, no reaction. Heading to the Southwest for a work project in December, aware to keep meds with him.

documents.title: Emergency Department Note (out of state)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT RECORD — date of service 12/21/2024

Arrival by EMS. 38-year-old man, history of generalized seizure disorder on levetiracetam and hypertension on lisinopril. Fever, rigors and shortness of breath came on abruptly. Dry cough started yesterday and is now productive of blood-streaked sputum. Wife at bedside: he got sick fast overnight and has been more and more confused. He is in New Mexico on a work assignment and helped with a prairie dog eradication effort last week. No travel outside the country.

Meds: levetiracetam 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 10 mg daily. NKDA.
PSH: tonsillectomy, appendectomy. Never smoker, social alcohol.

Vitals on arrival: T 39.6 C, HR 124, BP 92/58, RR 30.
Exam: obtunded. Frothy pink sputum with coughing. Diffuse crackles in both lung fields.

Sputum gram stain and culture: pleomorphic gram-negative rod.
CXR: bilateral alveolar infiltrates, necrotizing appearance.

Impression: pneumonic plague suspected given rodent exposure; hypoxic respiratory failure; presumed septic shock.
Disposition: intubated in the ED, admitted to ICU. Infection control and public health notified.

[Received by fax 1/10/2025 at patient's request. Scanned.]

documents.title: Theo is in the hospital
documents.author: patient
documents.body: This is Theo's wife writing from his account. He got very sick in New Mexico over the weekend and is in the ICU on a ventilator. They think it is plague from the prairie dog work. They are giving him IV antibiotics. I wanted his doctor to know. They are still giving his seizure medicine through the tube.

documents.title: RE: Theo is in the hospital
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thank you for letting me know, and I am so sorry. Please ask the team there to send us records when they can, and call us once he is home so we can see him soon after. Thinking of you both.

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called. Discharged 1/3 from the hospital in New Mexico and flew home with his wife on the 4th. Still on ciprofloxacin twice a day, last doses 1/7. Tired, mild cough, no fever, breathing ok walking around the house. Took Keppra and lisinopril throughout. Booked with PCP 1/14. Asked him to have the hospital fax records; he will call them.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily to complete 14 days of plague therapy

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen after hospitalization out of state. Only the ED record has reached us so far (received 1/10); the rest is from Theo and his wife.

On 12/21 he came into an ED in New Mexico by ambulance, febrile, hypotensive and confused, coughing blood-tinged sputum, about a week after working on a prairie dog control project. Intubated in the ED, ICU for septic shock. They told him the cultures grew plague (Y. pestis). Treated with IV gentamicin, off the ventilator on hospital day 5, moved to the floor, discharged 1/3 on oral ciprofloxacin 500 BID to finish 14 days total. Last dose 1/7. Levetiracetam was continued throughout and no seizures were reported; lisinopril was held while his pressure was low and restarted before discharge.

Now: energy maybe 60%, naps in the afternoon. Occasional dry cough, no more blood. No fever, chills or chest pain. Walks the dog a mile without stopping. Appetite back.

Exam: looks tired but comfortable. Afebrile. Pulse ox normal on room air. Lungs clear throughout, no crackles today. Heart regular. No calf tenderness or swelling. Neuro nonfocal, fully oriented.

A/P
1. Pneumonic plague, treated. Clinically recovering. Follow-up 2-view CXR in about 6 weeks to confirm clearing.
2. Hypoxic respiratory failure, resolved, on room air.
3. Post-ICU fatigue. Expect gradual improvement; return to field work as tolerated.
4. Seizure d/o: no events, continue levetiracetam 1000 BID.
5. HTN: restarted lisinopril 10, pressure fine today.
CBC, BMP today. Will chase the hospital discharge summary.

documents.title: Blood work after the hospital
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Theo, your blood counts have recovered and your kidney function and potassium are normal. The chest x-ray order is in for late February; any of our imaging sites can do it without an appointment.

documents.title: Records request follow-up
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Called the New Mexico hospital HIM department a second time for inpatient discharge summary. Told the request is in queue. Will try again in a month.

reports.text: PA and lateral chest. Comparison: none available. Lungs are clear. No consolidation, effusion or pneumothorax. Heart and mediastinal contours normal. Osseous structures intact.
reports.conclusion: No acute cardiopulmonary process. Previously reported bilateral infiltrates have cleared.

documents.title: CXR result note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Follow-up CXR clear. Plague pneumonia resolved. Message sent to pt.

documents.title: Chest x-ray
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good news, your chest x-ray is completely clear. Your lungs have healed from the infection.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam, also following up HTN and seizures.

Interval: recovered from the December plague pneumonia; Feb CXR clear. Back at work full time since March, mostly office and local surveys for now. Energy near normal. No cough. Still no discharge summary from NM despite two requests; not chasing further.

Seizures: none. Levetiracetam 1000 BID, no missed doses.
HTN: lisinopril 10 daily. No home readings.
Sleeping ok. Mood fine. Same 2-3 beers a week. Never smoked.
PHQ-2: 1.

Exam: NAD. HEENT normal. Neck no nodes or thyromegaly. CV RRR no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd soft, nontender, old appendectomy scar. Skin without rashes or worrisome lesions. Ext no edema. Neuro normal gait, strength symmetric.

A/P
1. Health maintenance, age 38: vaccines current through fall 2024 (Tdap 2020). No other screening due by age. Discussed sunscreen and tick checks with the field work.
2. HTN at goal. BMP today. Lisinopril 10 renewed, 90 days x 3.
3. Generalized seizure disorder, controlled. Levetiracetam 1000 BID renewed, 90 days x 3.
4. Plague pneumonia, resolved.
RTC 6 months for BP, sooner prn.

documents.title: ICU Discharge Summary
documents.author: critical care
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 12/23/2025, discharged 1/5/2026. Service: Pulmonary and Critical Care.

39M with generalized seizure disorder (well controlled on levetiracetam), hypertension, and pneumonic plague in Dec 2024, fully recovered. Brought in after being under cold water for several minutes before rescue. Hypoxemic on arrival in spite of supplemental O2.

On exam: tachypneic, using accessory muscles, crackles diffusely over both lungs. ABG: hypoxemia, widened A-a gradient. CXR: bilateral patchy opacities, heart size normal.

Diagnoses: ARDS with refractory hypoxemia; acute hypoxemic respiratory failure.

Course: intubated, lung-protective ventilation, proned for refractory hypoxemia. Oxygenation improved; extubated hospital day 6. Weaned to room air, ambulating before discharge. Levetiracetam continued, no seizures. Lisinopril held early, resumed.

Discharge meds: levetiracetam 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 10 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: pulmonary clinic in about 3 months with PFTs; PCP.

[Received 1/30/2026, filed to chart.]

documents.title: Theo in ICU again
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, it's Theo's wife again. He went under in very cold water on the 23rd and was pulled out after a few minutes. He's in the ICU at the regional hospital, on a breathing machine, and they say it's ARDS. He's improving a little each day. Just wanted you to know.

documents.title: RE: Theo in ICU again
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thank you for telling us. Glad he is improving. Please have the hospital send his discharge summary, and call to book a visit once he's home.

documents.title: Renewal request
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Mail-order asking for renewal of levetiracetam 1000 mg BID and lisinopril 10 mg daily (out of refills). Last seen 4/8/25; hospitalized Dec-Jan, discharge summary on file, same meds. Sent 90-day supply each, 1 refill. Pt needs a visit before further renewals; portal reminder sent.

reports.text: Good effort, acceptable and repeatable maneuvers. FVC, FEV1 and FEV1/FVC within normal limits. No obstruction or restriction pattern.
PA and lateral chest. Lungs clear. No effusion or pneumothorax. Normal heart size and mediastinum.

documents.title: Pulmonary clinic follow-up letter
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Re: Theo Lewandowski, seen 4/21/2026.

Thank you for allowing us to follow Mr. Lewandowski after his December ICU stay for ARDS following cold-water submersion. He reports breathing back to his baseline, hiking without limitation, no cough. On exam his lungs are clear. Spirometry today is normal and his chest film is clear.

Impression: recovered ARDS, no residual impairment on testing. No further pulmonary follow-up needed; we're glad to see him again if symptoms arise.

Meds per patient: levetiracetam 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 10 mg daily. NKDA.

Pulmonary Medicine
